Main topics: networking architecture (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), private endpoints, region and data residency constraints, KMS integration, audit logs, and pilot timeline. Customer leaning toward private deployment due to data residency and compliance needs; SE to provide example Terraform and connectivity guide; AE to send security pack and pricing.

Audit logs, SSO, RBAC and compliance (SOC2/ISO)

transcript: Meeting header: 2026-09-15 15:00 PDT - 58 minutes - Halcyon Insurance - Redwood Inference
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Halcyon Head of Cloud), Liam O'Connor (Halcyon Security), Rajiv Menon (Halcyon VP Product)
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate the time. Quick round-robin - I think everyone is listed but if you wanna say hi briefly that'd be great.
[00:10] Sofia Patel: Hi, Sofia here - lead infra. We're evaluating options for private inference, specifically a VPC/private endpoints setup. We're concerned about egress IPs and data residency.
[00:18] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv - product. We're focused on timeline and success criteria mainly: production latency under 150ms p99 for key routes, and no customer data leaving EU in plaintext.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Liam - security. SOC2 audited, we need key ownership and audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO. Also curious about certificate rotation and HSM support.

[00:45] Diego Alvarez: Great, thanks. Quick agenda - cover high-level deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), then dive network connectivity patterns, region constraints, and integration points like KMS and audit logs.

[01:02] Maya Chen: Just to set context - Halcyon had a pilot with an internal LLM but you're looking to move to a managed offering where we can deploy into your VPC or offer private endpoints. Is that right?

[01:10] Sofia Patel: Correct. We prefer customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink so we can control traffic egress; can't have traffic traverse public internet. Also need to know which AWS regions Redwood will support for private deployments.

[01:28] Diego Alvarez: Understood. For Redwood Private we support two primary connectivity patterns: VPC Peering (native peering connections) and PrivateLink / AWS Private Endpoints. Both keep data path within AWS backbone - peering is simpler network-wise but has some route table constraints; PrivateLink sits behind an endpoint service and can be easier for cross-account access without shared routes.
[01:45] Liam O'Connor: Does PrivateLink avoid the issue of overlapping CIDRs? We have some legacy ranges that overlap with partner networks.

[01:52] Diego Alvarez: Yes, PrivateLink avoids route overlap because it's an ENI-based endpoint. For peering you do need non-overlapping CIDRs or you must NAT. We'll send example CIDR ranges and guidance - and Terraform snippets to automate either approach.
[02:10] Sofia Patel: Okay. For peering, we also need to know egress IPs for allowlisting. Can you provide a stable set of IPs or are they dynamic?

[02:18] Maya Chen: For Dedicated pools we can provide a stable egress IP range per deployment; for hosted / multi-tenant it's less deterministic. Since you're interested in Private, we can either use static egress from Redwood-managed NAT in your VPC or integrate with your Transit Gateway. We'll include specifics in the connectivity doc.
[02:35] Rajiv Menon: Region-wise - we have EU customers; data residency is a hard requirement. Do you have private deployments in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1?

[02:44] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we support deployments in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for Private customers. There are also options to run on prem if needed - we have an on-prem bundle but need to discuss network/equipment sizing. Most customers do Private in EU regions to meet residency.
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: About encryption - we want customer-managed keys (CMKs) in our own KMS. Can Redwood support bring-your-own-KMS or HSM integration?

[03:13] Diego Alvarez: We support BYOK patterns. For AWS we can integrate with customer CMKs via IAM roles and grant decrypt access for the Redwood service role. HSM direct integration is available for enterprise customers with a private deployment - we can surface provider details in the security pack.
[03:30] Sofia Patel: Perfect. Also need to confirm audit logs retention - compliance requires 12 months of immutable logs and S3 access for our auditors.

[03:38] Maya Chen: We do audit log streaming to your account - CloudWatch or S3 ingestion is supported; retention and immutability policies can be implemented on your side. We'll include best practices and sample CloudFormation/Terraform to set that up.

[03:55] Diego Alvarez: Quick note about latency trade-offs - bringing the model closer to your VPC reduces hop count and jitter. But if you want failover to hosted for bursts, we can configure smart routing with fallbacks. We can set SLOs per-route. What's your expected throughput?
[04:10] Rajiv Menon: Initial traffic about 50 rps with spikes to 200 rps during peak hours. Latency SLO p50 ~ 60 - 80ms, p99 < 150ms. Cost is secondary to meeting these latency numbers for now.

[04:25] Diego Alvarez: That workload maps well to a small dedicated pool - we can size GPU instances accordingly. We'll recommend batching and KV cache settings to optimize tokens and cost once we know model type and seq lengths.
[04:40] Sofia Patel: Models - right now sticking with a fine-tuned open model (~7B). We might evaluate 13B later - will that affect network or region choices?
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: Mostly impacts compute sizing; region availability for larger instance types can vary. We can propose a fallback model plan so you don't lose availability during maintenance.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: SSO and RBAC - we need SAML integration with our IdP, and role-based access for dev vs prod. Can Redwood integrate with our existing SAML and SCIM provisioning?

[05:14] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. For Private deployments we can configure a private control plane that respects your SAML IdP. We'll share docs on attribute mappings.
[05:30] Sofia Patel: One more on networking: do you support AWS Transit Gateway? We centralize routing through TGW and want a TGW-compatible pattern.

[05:38] Diego Alvarez: We do. Customers commonly use TGW and we can peer or attach via Transit Gateway attachments; there are some route propagation gotchas we'll document. We'll include an example architecture for TGW + PrivateLink.
[06:00] Rajiv Menon: Onboarding timeline - if we like the pilot, what's the typical time to production for Private?

[06:07] Maya Chen: Typical pilot is 4-6 weeks for Private: week 1 network & account setup, week 2 provisioning and test endpoints, weeks 3-4 pilot workloads and tuning, then roll to prod after validation. If you want faster we can do a parallel hosted pilot for feature validation while Private infra is procured.
[06:25] Sofia Patel: Budget authority - procurement will need an estimate. Can you do a T-shirt sizing now?
[06:30] Maya Chen: Yes - we'll provide T-shirt sizing and a cost estimate for dedicated GPU pools and expected token/unit costs, plus an itemized pilot SOW.

[06:40] Diego Alvarez: Security question - do you need the control plane inside your account or can it be Redwood-managed with VPC peering? Some customers insist on local control plane for extra compliance.
[06:50] Liam O'Connor: For now Redwood-managed control plane is OK as long as we have audit logs and can't see customer PII. But if auditors push we might require on-prem control plane later.
[07:05] Diego Alvarez: Noted. We offer a private control plane option for enterprise customers; that'll be in the enterprise package and we can include it in the SOW if needed.
[07:20] Sofia Patel: Any limitations around multi-region replication? We want failover between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 without moving data out of EU.

[07:28] Diego Alvarez: You can have deployments in both regions with internal replication that stays in-region; failover routing is region-aware. We'll show an example blue/green roll and how to replicate KV cache warming across regions safely.
[07:45] Rajiv Menon: Compliance - do you have ISO 27001 in addition to SOC2?
[07:50] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II and are working on ISO; we'll share current compliance artifacts in the security pack.
[08:05] Sofia Patel: Okay, can you also include pen test reports and data handling policies for model inputs? That's a common ask from auditors.
[08:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include pen test summaries and our PII handling policy. Also, examples of data flow diagrams showing which components see customer plaintext.

[08:30] Diego Alvarez: Small nit - for KMS when you provide CMKs we'll need a cross-account key policy or a grant so Redwood services can decrypt. We can provide a sample policy; some customers rotate keys monthly and we support rotation without downtime if configured properly.
[08:50] Liam O'Connor: Key rotation is a must. Also need to ensure logs show key usage events for audits.
[08:56] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely - CloudTrail + key usage logs can be delivered to your account. We'll document retention and immutable S3 setups.

[09:10] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we open up to questions: we will send security pack, connectivity guide (peering and PrivateLink), example Terraform, sample IAM/KMS policies, initial pricing and SOW. SE will run deep-dive network session next week. Anything to add?
[09:25] Rajiv Menon: Add a small benchmark run - 50 rps, 13B model emulation, p99 target, just to validate sizing.
[09:32] Diego Alvarez: We'll propose a short benchmark during pilot - can do synthetic load and replay test with your typical prompts. We'll need sample prompts and average sequence lengths.
[09:45] Sofia Patel: We'll share sample prompts and token distributions after the call.
[09:50] Liam O'Connor: Question about legal - data processing agreement and subprocessor list?
[09:57] Maya Chen: We'll include the DPA and subprocessor list in the security pack; procurement typically reviews that in parallel with tech onboarding.
[10:10] Sofia Patel: Any blockers you foresee?

[10:15] Diego Alvarez: Nothing immediate - overlapping CIDR can be a blocker for peering but that's solvable with PrivateLink or NAT. Access approvals and procurement timelines can move faster or slower depending on your org.
[10:30] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. Let's lock the tech deep-dive for Thursday 2026-09-17 10am CET.
[10:38] Maya Chen: I'll send the calendar invite and prep notes. Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[10:45] Sofia Patel: Thanks, appreciate it.
[57:12] End of recording
